SAFETY.TITLE: Safety protection
SAFETY.DESCRIPTION: Requests with safety records, counted once per user message in this period. Checks and retries are grouped together.
SAFETY.ERROR: Safety data could not be loaded.
SAFETY.COMPARISON_NOTE: Evaluation only: compare basic safety decisions for the same attempt, stage and content. Business scope decisions are not compared with AWS basic safety. Different content, missing results and AWS-blocked original outputs are not comparable. Disagreement needs review; it does not prove a mistake.

MODES.hybrid_shadow: AWS Guardrails + Custom Guard · Evaluation on

SAFETY.USAGE: Custom reviewer usage (separate from Bot): {input} input tokens including cache · {output} output tokens · {missing} checks with missing usage. Reviewer costs are not included in cost estimates.
SAFETY.TREND_NOTE: Blocks are part of recorded requests. Review issues include evaluation failures; they are not safety violations. Dates use the first recorded check in this period.
SAFETY.REASONS_NOTE: Enforced blocks only. A request can have more than one reason.
SAFETY.EVIDENCE_NOTE: Recorded checks, including retries. Provider summaries prioritise blocks, then review issues. No recorded block does not prove a complete review or successful delivery. Message content is not stored in this report; open the conversation for context.
SAFETY.COUNTING_NOTE: Counts cover only safety records within the selected period, not all incoming messages. Older records without a message ID are grouped by attempt. No recorded block does not prove a complete review or reply delivery. A missing or skipped review counts as an issue when it was required. Downstream reviews made unnecessary by an enforced block in the same attempt do not count as issues; they remain not comparable.
SAFETY.DIMENSIONS_NOTE: Blocked requests by responsibility. Requests are counted once overall; responsibility counts can overlap. Historical combined checks remain separate.
